lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Discussion or problem seminar: equal angles and proportional sides

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: One approach is shown. There is at least one other that works.

items.prompt: Two triangles share two pairs of equal angles. Similar?

steps: The third angles must match too.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: For each, name a second method before you solve it.

items.prompt: Under a dilation, a line that does not pass through the centre of dilation …
choices: is mapped to a line with slope multiplied by the scale factor
is mapped to a perpendicular line
is mapped to a parallel line

items.prompt: Dilate the point (8, -5) about the origin with scale factor 5. Give the image.
A figure is dilated so that a side of length 8 becomes a side of length 40. What is the scale factor, and what happens to the figure's area?
choices: scale factor 5; the area is multiplied by 5
scale factor 1/5; the area is multiplied by 25
scale factor 5; the area is multiplied by 25
scale factor 32; the area is multiplied by 25

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Triangle ABC has ∠A = 35° and ∠B = 52°. Triangle DEF has ∠D = 35° and ∠E = 52°. Are the triangles similar, and on what grounds?
choices: Yes, by AA similarity: two pairs of congruent angles force the third pair to be congruent as well.
No; angle information alone never establishes similarity.
Yes, but only if a pair of corresponding sides is also known to be congruent.

items.prompt: Under a dilation, a segment not through the centre, under a dilation with scale factor k …
choices: is mapped to a segment of the same length
is mapped to a segment k² times as long
is mapped to a perpendicular segment k times as long
is mapped to a parallel segment k times as long

items.prompt: Dilate the point (-2, -2) about the origin with scale factor 3. Give the image.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Argue for one method over another. Say what makes it better, not just that it is.

items.prompt: A figure is dilated so that a side of length 19 becomes a side of length 38. What is the scale factor, and what happens to the figure's area?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Triangle ABC has ∠A = 32° and ∠B = 46°. Triangle DEF has ∠D = 32° and ∠E = 46°. Are the triangles similar, and on what grounds?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
